questions.q: How many bones are there in the adult human skeleton?
questions.explain: A newborn has about 270–300 bony parts; many fuse during growth, leaving 206 in the adult.

questions.q: Which is the longest bone in the body?
questions.explain: The femur runs from the hip to the knee. It is also the strongest bone in the body.

questions.q: Which part of the skull forms the protective case around the brain?
questions.explain: The cranium encloses the brain. The mandible and maxilla are the jaws, and the hyoid sits in the neck.

questions.q: How many pairs of ribs are there?
questions.explain: Twelve pairs: seven true ribs, three false ribs and two floating ribs.

questions.q: Which vertebrae are found in the neck?
questions.explain: There are seven cervical vertebrae, C1 to C7. C1 is the atlas and C2 is the axis.

questions.q: What is the kneecap called?
questions.explain: The patella sits in the tendon of quadriceps femoris and improves its leverage over the knee.

questions.q: Which bone is the collarbone?
questions.explain: The clavicle links the upper limb to the trunk at the sternoclavicular joint.

questions.q: What is the heel bone called?
questions.explain: The calcaneus is the largest tarsal bone; the calcaneal (Achilles) tendon attaches to it.

questions.q: Where is the radius?
options: On the thumb side of the forearm
On the little-finger side of the forearm
questions.explain: In the anatomical position the radius is lateral, on the thumb side; the ulna is medial.

questions.q: What type of joint is the shoulder joint?
questions.explain: The head of the humerus fits the glenoid cavity of the scapula, giving the widest range of movement of any joint.

questions.q: What type of joint is the elbow joint between the humerus and the ulna?
questions.explain: A hinge joint allows flexion and extension only.

questions.q: Which tissue joins muscle to bone?
questions.explain: Tendons join muscle to bone. Ligaments join bone to bone.

questions.q: Which is the main muscle of breathing?
questions.explain: When the diaphragm contracts it flattens, the chest gets bigger and air is drawn into the lungs.

questions.q: Which muscle group straightens (extends) the knee?
questions.explain: The four heads of quadriceps femoris pull on the patella and the patellar ligament to extend the knee.

questions.q: Which muscle bends the elbow and turns the palm upwards?
questions.explain: Biceps brachii flexes the elbow and is the strongest supinator of the forearm. Triceps straightens the elbow.

questions.q: Which muscle forms the rounded contour of the shoulder?
questions.explain: The deltoid covers the shoulder joint and abducts the arm. It is a common site for injections.

questions.q: Which muscles form the calf?
questions.explain: Gastrocnemius and soleus join the calcaneal (Achilles) tendon and point the foot down (plantarflexion).

questions.q: How many chambers does the human heart have?
questions.explain: Two atria receive blood and two ventricles pump it out.

questions.q: Which chamber pumps oxygenated blood to the body?
questions.explain: The left ventricle pumps blood into the aorta. Its wall is the thickest of the four chambers.

questions.q: Which vessels carry blood away from the heart?
questions.explain: Arteries carry blood away from the heart; veins carry it back. This is true whether or not the blood is oxygenated.

questions.q: Which vessels carry deoxygenated blood from the heart to the lungs?
questions.explain: The pulmonary arteries are the only arteries after birth that carry deoxygenated blood.

questions.q: Which is the largest artery in the body?
questions.explain: The aorta leaves the left ventricle and carries oxygenated blood to the whole body.

questions.q: Which vein returns blood from the lower body to the heart?
questions.explain: The inferior vena cava drains the legs, pelvis and abdomen into the right atrium.

questions.q: What is the natural pacemaker of the heart?
questions.explain: The SA node in the wall of the right atrium starts each heartbeat.

questions.q: Where is the radial pulse felt?
options: At the wrist, on the thumb side
On the top of the foot
questions.explain: The radial artery lies just under the skin at the front of the wrist, lateral to the flexor tendons.

questions.q: Which blood cells carry oxygen?
questions.explain: Red blood cells (erythrocytes) are packed with haemoglobin, which binds oxygen.

questions.q: Which part of the blood helps it to clot?
questions.explain: Platelets stick together at a damaged vessel and start the clotting process.

questions.q: Where are gases exchanged in the lungs?
questions.explain: Oxygen and carbon dioxide cross the thin walls of the alveoli and the capillaries around them.

questions.q: What is the windpipe called?
questions.explain: The trachea runs from the larynx to the main bronchi and is held open by C-shaped rings of cartilage.

questions.q: How many lobes does the right lung have?
questions.explain: The right lung has upper, middle and lower lobes. The left lung has two, to make room for the heart.

questions.q: What is the voice box called?
questions.explain: The larynx contains the vocal folds, which vibrate to make sound.

questions.q: Which flap covers the entrance to the larynx when you swallow?
questions.explain: The epiglottis helps stop food and drink going down the wrong way into the airway.

questions.q: Which organ makes bile?
questions.explain: The liver makes bile; the gallbladder stores and concentrates it. Bile helps to digest fats.

questions.q: Where does most digestion and absorption of food take place?
questions.explain: The small intestine is about 6 metres long and its lining is folded into villi to absorb nutrients.

questions.q: Which tube carries food from the pharynx to the stomach?
questions.explain: The oesophagus moves food down by waves of muscle contraction (peristalsis).

questions.q: What is the first part of the small intestine?
questions.explain: The duodenum receives bile and pancreatic juice. It is followed by the jejunum and then the ileum.

questions.q: In which part of the abdomen is the appendix usually found?
questions.explain: The appendix hangs from the caecum in the right iliac fossa, so appendicitis pain settles in the right lower quadrant.

questions.q: In which part of the abdomen is the spleen?
questions.explain: The spleen lies under the left ribs 9 to 11, behind the stomach.

questions.q: Which organ makes insulin?
questions.explain: Beta cells in the pancreatic islets (of Langerhans) make insulin, which lowers blood glucose.

questions.q: Which gland is often called the "master gland"?
questions.explain: The pituitary gland, under the brain, controls many other endocrine glands. It is itself controlled by the hypothalamus.

questions.q: Where is the thyroid gland?
options: At the front of the neck, below the larynx
questions.explain: Its two lobes lie on either side of the trachea, joined by an isthmus in front of the upper tracheal rings.

questions.q: Which organs filter the blood to make urine?
questions.explain: Each kidney has about a million nephrons that filter the blood.

questions.q: Which tube carries urine from each kidney to the bladder?
questions.explain: There are two ureters, one from each kidney. The single urethra carries urine out of the bladder.

questions.q: What is the basic working unit of the kidney?
questions.explain: The nephron filters the blood and adjusts what it filters. The glomerulus is only its filtering knot of capillaries.

questions.q: Which part of the brain coordinates balance and smooth movement?
questions.explain: The cerebellum sits at the back of the skull, under the cerebrum.

questions.q: Which part of the brainstem contains the centres that control breathing and heart rate?
questions.explain: The medulla oblongata is the lowest part of the brainstem and joins the spinal cord.

questions.q: How many pairs of cranial nerves are there?
questions.explain: Twelve pairs of cranial nerves leave the brain. Thirty-one pairs of spinal nerves leave the spinal cord.

questions.q: How many pairs of spinal nerves are there?
questions.explain: 8 cervical, 12 thoracic, 5 lumbar, 5 sacral and 1 coccygeal pair.

questions.q: What is a nerve cell called?
questions.explain: A neuron has a cell body, dendrites that receive signals and an axon that sends them on.

questions.q: Which part of the eye controls how much light enters it?
questions.explain: The iris changes the size of the pupil: smaller in bright light, larger in dim light.

questions.q: Which layer of the eye contains the light-sensitive cells?
questions.explain: Rods and cones in the retina turn light into nerve signals carried by the optic nerve.

questions.q: Which is the smallest bone in the body?
questions.explain: The stapes, in the middle ear, passes vibrations to the inner ear. It is about 3 mm long.

questions.q: What is the largest organ of the body?
questions.explain: In an adult the skin covers about 1.5 to 2 square metres. It protects the body, helps to control temperature and senses touch.

questions.q: In the anatomical position, which way do the palms face?
questions.explain: The body stands upright, facing forwards, arms by the sides, with the palms facing forwards.

questions.q: What does "proximal" mean?
options: Closer to the trunk or point of attachment
Further from the trunk or point of attachment
questions.explain: The elbow is proximal to the wrist. The opposite is distal.

questions.q: Which plane divides the body into left and right parts?
questions.explain: The median sagittal plane runs down the midline; the coronal plane divides front from back.

questions.q: What does "anterior" mean?
questions.explain: Anterior (ventral) means towards the front. The opposite is posterior (dorsal).

questions.q: Which nerve is most at risk in a fracture of the surgical neck of the humerus?
questions.explain: The axillary nerve winds round the surgical neck. Damage weakens the deltoid and numbs the skin over it (the "regimental badge" area).

questions.q: A fracture of the shaft of the humerus causes wrist drop. Which nerve has been injured?
questions.explain: The radial nerve runs in the radial groove on the back of the humerus and supplies the extensors of the wrist and fingers.

questions.q: Which nerve passes through the carpal tunnel?
questions.explain: Compression of the median nerve in the carpal tunnel causes tingling in the thumb, index and middle fingers.

questions.q: Which muscles make up the rotator cuff?
options: Supraspinatus, infraspinatus, teres minor and subscapularis
Deltoid, supraspinatus, teres major and subscapularis
Infraspinatus, teres major, latissimus dorsi and supraspinatus
Pectoralis minor, subscapularis, teres minor and deltoid
questions.explain: Remember "SITS". Their tendons blend with the capsule and hold the head of the humerus in the glenoid cavity.

questions.q: Which rotator cuff muscle starts abduction of the arm?
questions.explain: Supraspinatus starts abduction; the deltoid takes over after about the first 15 degrees.

questions.q: Damage to the long thoracic nerve causes which sign?
questions.explain: The long thoracic nerve supplies serratus anterior, which holds the scapula against the chest wall.

questions.q: A fall on the outstretched hand causes tenderness in the anatomical snuffbox. Which bone is most likely fractured?
questions.explain: Its blood supply enters at the distal end, so a fracture through its waist can leave the proximal part without blood (avascular necrosis).

questions.q: Erb's palsy, with the arm in the "waiter's tip" position, follows injury to which roots of the brachial plexus?
questions.explain: An injury to the upper roots (C5, C6) weakens the shoulder abductors, lateral rotators and elbow flexors. Injury to C8 and T1 is Klumpke's palsy.

questions.q: In the femoral triangle, what is the order of structures from lateral to medial?
questions.explain: Remember "NAVY": nerve, artery, vein, then the empty space and lymphatics of the femoral canal.

questions.q: Which nerve is at risk in a fracture of the neck of the fibula?
questions.explain: It winds round the neck of the fibula. Injury causes foot drop and numbness on the top of the foot.

questions.q: Which ligament stops the tibia sliding forwards on the femur?
questions.explain: The anterior cruciate ligament is tested with the anterior drawer and Lachman tests.

questions.q: Where does the great saphenous vein pass at the ankle?
options: In front of the medial malleolus
In front of the lateral malleolus
questions.explain: It is reliably found in front of the medial malleolus, which is why it can be used for emergency venous access.

questions.q: Where is the dorsalis pedis pulse felt?
options: On the top of the foot, lateral to the tendon of extensor hallucis longus
questions.explain: The dorsalis pedis artery continues the anterior tibial artery onto the foot.

questions.q: Where is the posterior tibial pulse felt?
options: On the top of the foot
questions.explain: The posterior tibial artery passes behind the medial malleolus into the sole of the foot.

questions.q: Which intramuscular injection site is preferred in adults because it lies away from the sciatic nerve and large vessels?
options: The centre of the buttock (dorsogluteal site)
questions.explain: The ventrogluteal site is found using the greater trochanter, the anterior superior iliac spine and the iliac crest.

questions.q: At what vertebral level does the spinal cord usually end in adults?
questions.explain: Below this the vertebral canal holds the cauda equina, which is why a lumbar puncture is done lower down.

questions.q: Between which vertebrae is a lumbar puncture usually performed?
questions.explain: A line joining the tops of the iliac crests crosses the L4 spinous process, a useful landmark.

questions.q: Which nerves supply the diaphragm?
questions.explain: "C3, 4 and 5 keep the diaphragm alive." A high cervical spinal injury can stop breathing.

questions.q: Through which opening and at what level does the inferior vena cava pass through the diaphragm?
options: The sternocostal triangle, behind the xiphoid process
questions.explain: Remember "I 8 10 Eggs At 12": inferior vena cava T8, oesophagus T10, aorta T12.

questions.q: At what vertebral level does the oesophagus pass through the diaphragm?
questions.explain: It passes through a sling of fibres from the right crus of the diaphragm.

questions.q: At what level does the trachea divide into the two main bronchi?
options: T4–T5, at the level of the sternal angle
C6, at the level of the cricoid cartilage
questions.explain: The sternal angle also marks the second costal cartilage and the beginning and end of the aortic arch.

questions.q: Why does an inhaled foreign body more often enter the right main bronchus?
options: It is wider, shorter and more vertical than the left
It is narrower and longer than the left
It lies in front of the oesophagus
questions.explain: The left main bronchus is longer and more horizontal because it passes under the aortic arch.

questions.q: In adults, where is the narrowest part of the larynx?
options: Between the vocal folds (the rima glottidis)
In the vestibule above the vestibular folds
questions.explain: This is why an object too big to pass the vocal folds can block the airway completely.

questions.q: Which valve lies between the left atrium and the left ventricle?
questions.explain: The mitral valve has two cusps. The tricuspid valve, with three, lies between the right atrium and the right ventricle.

questions.q: Where is the apex beat normally felt?
options: Left fifth intercostal space, in the mid-clavicular line
Right second intercostal space, at the sternal edge
Left second intercostal space, at the sternal edge
questions.explain: A displaced apex beat can be a sign of an enlarged heart.

questions.q: Which artery most often supplies the sinoatrial node?
questions.explain: In about 60% of people the sinoatrial nodal artery is a branch of the right coronary artery.

questions.q: Which part of the conducting system delays the impulse between the atria and the ventricles?
questions.explain: The delay lets the atria finish emptying before the ventricles contract.

questions.q: Which unpaired branch of the abdominal aorta supplies the stomach, liver and spleen?
questions.explain: The coeliac trunk leaves the aorta at T12 and divides into the left gastric, common hepatic and splenic arteries.

questions.q: Which veins join to form the hepatic portal vein?
options: The superior mesenteric and splenic veins
The inferior vena cava and the renal vein
The right and left gastric veins
questions.explain: They join behind the neck of the pancreas. The portal vein carries blood from the gut to the liver.

questions.q: Which artery is usually torn in an extradural haematoma after a blow to the side of the head (the pterion)?
questions.explain: The skull is thin at the pterion and the artery runs just inside it, between the bone and the dura.

questions.q: In the fetus, the ductus arteriosus connects which two vessels?
options: The pulmonary trunk and the aorta
The umbilical vein and the inferior vena cava
The aorta and the inferior vena cava
questions.explain: It lets blood bypass the lungs before birth. Afterwards it closes and becomes the ligamentum arteriosum.

questions.q: In the fetal heart, the foramen ovale lets blood pass from where to where?
questions.explain: It closes at birth, when pressure in the left atrium rises, leaving the fossa ovalis.

questions.q: Where does the thoracic duct drain?
options: Into the junction of the left internal jugular and left subclavian veins
questions.explain: It returns lymph from most of the body to the blood at the left venous angle.

questions.q: Which lymph nodes drain most of the lymph from the breast?
questions.explain: About 75% drains to the axillary nodes, the rest mainly to the parasternal nodes.

questions.q: What lies in the free edge of the lesser omentum?
options: Hepatic portal vein, hepatic artery proper and bile duct
questions.explain: These form the portal triad. Pressing them between finger and thumb (Pringle's manoeuvre) controls bleeding from the liver.

questions.q: Where is McBurney's point?
options: One-third of the way from the anterior superior iliac spine to the umbilicus
Halfway between the umbilicus and the pubic symphysis
At the tip of the ninth costal cartilage
Two-thirds of the way from the anterior superior iliac spine to the umbilicus
questions.explain: It marks the usual position of the base of the appendix, where tenderness is greatest in appendicitis.

questions.q: Which cells in the stomach make hydrochloric acid and intrinsic factor?
questions.explain: Chief cells make pepsinogen and G cells make gastrin.

questions.q: Where is vitamin B12 mainly absorbed?
questions.explain: It is absorbed bound to intrinsic factor, so removing the terminal ileum can cause B12 deficiency.

questions.q: Which hormone do the beta cells of the pancreatic islets make?
questions.explain: Alpha cells make glucagon and delta cells make somatostatin.

questions.q: Which part of the nephron reabsorbs most of the filtered water, sodium and glucose?
questions.explain: It reabsorbs about two-thirds of the filtered water and sodium, and normally all of the glucose.

questions.q: Antidiuretic hormone (ADH) mainly acts on which part of the nephron?
options: Ascending limb of the loop of Henle
questions.explain: ADH inserts water channels (aquaporins) so more water is reabsorbed and the urine is more concentrated.

questions.q: Why is the ureter at risk during a hysterectomy?
options: It passes under the uterine artery
It passes over the uterine artery
It runs through the inguinal canal
questions.explain: Remember "water under the bridge": the ureter (water) passes under the uterine artery (the bridge).

questions.q: Which is the longest part of the male urethra?
questions.explain: The spongy urethra is about 15 cm long and runs through the corpus spongiosum.

questions.q: Which cranial nerve supplies the muscles of facial expression?
questions.explain: Damage to the facial nerve, as in Bell's palsy, causes weakness of one side of the face.

questions.q: When the tongue is stuck out it points towards the side of a nerve lesion. Which nerve is damaged?
questions.explain: The hypoglossal nerve supplies the muscles of the tongue. The healthy side pushes the tongue over to the weak side.

questions.q: Which cranial nerve supplies the lateral rectus muscle of the eye?
questions.explain: Remember "LR6 SO4": lateral rectus by VI, superior oblique by IV, all the others by III.

questions.q: Which muscle is supplied by the accessory nerve (XI)?
questions.explain: The accessory nerve supplies trapezius and sternocleidomastoid. It is tested by asking the patient to shrug.

questions.q: Which area of the brain is needed to produce speech, usually in the left hemisphere?
questions.explain: Damage here causes slow, effortful speech with good understanding (expressive aphasia).

questions.q: In which gyrus is the primary motor cortex?
questions.explain: The postcentral gyrus, just behind it, is the primary sensory cortex.

questions.q: Which layer of the meninges lies directly on the brain?
questions.explain: From outside in: dura, arachnoid, pia. Cerebrospinal fluid fills the subarachnoid space between the arachnoid and pia.

questions.q: Where is most cerebrospinal fluid made?
questions.explain: It is reabsorbed into the venous sinuses through the arachnoid granulations.

questions.q: Injury to the left recurrent laryngeal nerve causes hoarseness. Which structure does this nerve hook under?
questions.explain: The right recurrent laryngeal nerve hooks under the right subclavian artery instead.

questions.q: Drooping of the upper eyelid, a small pupil and loss of sweating on one side of the face (Horner's syndrome) result from damage to what?
questions.explain: The sympathetic supply to the eye and face can be cut, for example, by a tumour at the apex of the lung.

questions.q: A pituitary tumour pressing on the optic chiasm typically causes what?
options: Loss of both outer (temporal) halves of the visual field
Loss of the same half of the visual field in both eyes
A blind spot in the centre of vision
questions.explain: The fibres that cross at the chiasm come from the nasal halves of the retinas, which see the temporal fields (bitemporal hemianopia).
